subject: Feasibility & exception path for Acme Health on‑prem pilot
messages:
From: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Sarah Winters <sarah@acmehealth.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Feasibility & exception path for Acme Health on‑prem pilot

Hi all,

Acme Health is asking for a short pilot to run our LLM inference inside their datacenter (air‑gapped rack) for a clinical NLP workload. They need confirmation that we can:

- meet their SOC/security artifacts (they attached a filtered audit worksheet)
- support a single‑customer on‑prem deployment for 6 months as an exception to our standard Hosted/Dedicated flows
- provide an ops staffing plan for oncall and quarterly patching

Quick context: they expect ~20 qps sustained during business hours, spikes to 80 qps, and a hard requirement that keys never leave their KMS. Procurement also wants an expected procurement timeline (they said ~6–8 weeks after SOW).

Immediate asks:
1) Marcus — can you sketch a minimal architecture (GPU profile, network, KV cache considerations) and an estimated engineering effort (FTE weeks) for an MVP?
2) Grace — what compliance docs and evidence would we need to sign off on a short‑term exception? Any gating questions?
3) Laura — ops/CS — what oncall/staffing model do we propose for a single customer on‑prem pilot?

I attached the Acme worksheet (acme_audit_requirements.xlsx) and a quick deploy sketch (mvp_deploy_sketch.pdf).

Goal: come back with a recommended pathway (supported, supported-with-guardrails, or not-suggested) and a realistic timeline by EOD Friday so I can update Sarah and Procurement.

Thanks,
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Sarah Winters <sarah@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T12:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Feasibility & exception path for Acme Health on‑prem pilot

Dylan —

Thanks for the brief. High level thoughts (MVP scope):

- Hardware: 2x A40/A10G (or 1x A100 40GB) to start, node pool with single‑tenant placement. If Acme wants redundancy across racks we need +1 node.
- Networking: outbound-control plane to our private control plane must be allowed to a small egress set; if truly air‑gapped we need offline package + customer‑run control plane proxy (adds ~2 weeks).
- Model: suggest quantized 16-bit variant of the recommended model (we'll provide vetted quantization profile) to reduce memory and enable dense batching.
- KV cache: implement local disk-backed prefix cache for warm sessions; for 80 qps spikes batching strategy will be essential.

Estimated engineering effort for an MVP (safe):
- 4 weeks (1 eng, full time) for packaging runtime + install scripts + basic telemetry integration (no auto‑scaling)
- 2 weeks (0.5 eng) for quantization verification and perf tuning on customer hardware
- 1 week (0.5 eng) ops handover & runbook

Risk flags: KMS integration is nontrivial (depends on HSM/KMS vendor). If keys cannot be used by our runtime we must run entirely within customer vault with a restricted control plane—this is a larger integration (+3–4 weeks).

Attachment: I will upload a short arch diagram separately (mvp_deploy_sketch.pdf already sent).

Recommendation: supported-with-guardrails. We can do a time‑boxed pilot with documented exceptions and a rollback plan.

— Marcus
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
From: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Sarah Winters <sarah@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Feasibility & exception path for Acme Health on‑prem pilot

Dylan / team —

Reviewed the Acme worksheet quickly. Top compliance asks we need to validate for a short pilot:

- Evidence of secure deployment steps (install checklist, patch cadence),
- Attestation we do not persist PHI in our hosted control plane logs (we need log redaction or no‑log mode),
- KMS/HSM alignment (vendor, key escrow policy),
- SOC2 evidence for our packaging process (packaging and build pipeline hardening).

Gating questions for the pilot:
1) Can Acme accept an NDA amendment for short‑term exception liability and audit window?
2) Will they provide a secure transfer mechanism for the runtime package (signed binaries + attestations)?
3) Do they require continuous telemetry? If yes, that needs waivers (we can do batched telemetry or on‑demand pull).

If answers align, compliance can sign off on a limited pilot with the following controls:
- No persistent telemetry to our hosted plane; only batched, customer‑cleared diagnostics,
- Time‑boxed certificate for the pilot with documented rollback,
- Periodic external audit checkpoint (weekly for first month).

Estimate: legal & compliance coordination ~2 weeks to finalize amendment (concurrent with engineering).

— Grace
Director, Trust & Compliance
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Sarah Winters <sarah@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-27T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Feasibility & exception path for Acme Health on‑prem pilot

Folks —

Operational considerations for a single‑customer on‑prem pilot:

- Runbook & escalation: need a dedicated runbook + a named oncall engineer for the pilot window. Ops can allocate 0.2 FTE (8 hours/week) for monitoring but requires an escalation path to Marcus for infra issues.
- Patching: recommend a monthly patch window, with security hotfixes outside schedule. Ops will require at least 2 weeks notice for any kernel/container changes.
- Support SLAs: for pilot propose 24x5 phone & email with 4‑hour response for P1. Any 24x7 requirement increases staffing to ~0.6 FTE.
- Billing/credits: recommend a pilot credit to cover ops intensity (suggest 20% platform credit).

I'll draft a minimal runbook + oncall RACI by Thursday.

— Laura
Head of Customer Operations
From: Sarah Winters <sarah@acmehealth.com>
To: dylan.brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2027-04-28T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Feasibility & exception path for Acme Health on‑prem pilot

Hi Dylan —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and detailed responses. A few clarifications from Acme side:

- We can provide a signed transfer mechanism and a dedicated rack with required GPUs; procurement confirms budget and wants the SOW + legal amendment this month.
- KMS vendor is Vault by HashiCorp (we can provide access patterns and a contact).
- Telemetry: we prefer batched diagnostics only; no continuous PII/PHI export.
- Timeline: procurement expects SOW signature within 4 weeks if we can finalize the amendment this week.

Next steps from our side: procurement will send a short SOW draft by EOD Monday; can you confirm whether the packaging + install path (Marcus's estimate) and compliance amendment (Grace's estimate) can align with their 4‑week expectation?

Appreciate the team moving quickly — Sarah
Director of Engineering, Acme Health
